findings.evidence: Moments.lean:56 `memLp_two_algebraMap_eval_measureT {𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜]`, docstring at Measure.lean:186 "the form consumed by the family-generic orthogonality-to-Hilbert-basis bridge"; grep shows it has no consumer. WeightedOrthogonalBasis.lean:167-174 is 𝕜-generic.
findings.fix: Generalize to `polynomialEvalChebyshevLp (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] : ℝ[X] →ₗ[ℝ] Lp 𝕜 2 measureT` built from `memLp_two_algebraMap_eval_measureT`, and add ℝ specializations as in `inner_normalizedChebyshevTLp_real`.
findings.issue: `polynomialEvalChebyshevLp` is fixed at `Lp ℝ 2 measureT`, but the mode API it pairs with is `normalizedChebyshevTLp (𝕜) [RCLike 𝕜]` and the completeness target it feeds, `hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure`, takes `(Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range (bareNormalizedLp (𝕜 := 𝕜) ...)))ᗮ = ⊥`. The 𝕜-generic prerequisite `memLp_two_algebraMap_eval_measureT` already exists for exactly this and is left unused, so the exposed span/orthogonality results cannot be applied at 𝕜 ≠ ℝ.

findings.evidence: The file's own sibling convention does this: `inner_normalizedChebyshevTLp` (Measure.lean:236) is stated at inner-product level and proved via `MeasureTheory.L2.inner_def` (Measure.lean:248) so consumers never unfold `toLp`.
findings.fix: Add `inner_polynomialEvalChebyshevLp (g : Lp ℝ 2 measureT) (q) : inner ℝ g (polynomialEvalChebyshevLp q) = ∫ x, g x * q.eval x ∂measureT` and restate the corollary as a moment-vanishing statement.
findings.issue: No lemma relates `inner g (polynomialEvalChebyshevLp q)` to `∫ x, g x * q.eval x ∂measureT`, so the advertised product ("vanishing polynomial moments", line 100-101) is not actually reachable without unfolding through `coeFn_polynomialEvalChebyshevLp` and `L2.inner_def` at every use site.

summary: The surface is minimal and bodies are unexposed, but the new evaluation map is ℝ-only while every neighbouring layer (normalizedChebyshevTLp 𝕜, memLp_two_algebraMap_eval_measureT, hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure) is 𝕜-generic, and the file never delivers the integral/moment form its own docstrings promise.
